places.name: Île Saint-Louis, Paris
places.what: Her father, the organist Claude Jacquet, held the post at Saint-Louis-en-l’Île, and the dedication of her first book mentions a long retreat at her father’s house. No source consulted gives the family’s address during her childhood; the island is inferred from her father’s post.

sources.title: Dedication of Les Pièces de clavessin (1687), transcribed in the Philidor catalogue, collection EJG.recueil.01
Catherine Cessac, Elisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre, France Archives

places.name: Paris
places.what: Baptised in Paris on 17 March 1665. The sources consulted do not name the parish or give a birth date; the point marks the city.

sources.title: Catherine Cessac, Elisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre, France Archives (Recueil des Commémorations 2015)
Radio France, biography of Élisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre
Wikipedia coordinate record: Paris

places.name: Court of Louis XIV (Versailles)
places.what: Titon du Tillet wrote that she was barely fifteen when she appeared at court and that Madame de Montespan kept her three or four years; Cessac gives three, and Radio France dates her entry to the court to 1682, at seventeen. The sources consulted do not name the residence, and the start year is counted as fifteen years from her baptism. Versailles is used here to stand for the court.

sources.title: Titon du Tillet, Le Parnasse françois (1732), entry CCXLIX, p. 635

places.name: Rue Guillaume (now rue Budé), Île Saint-Louis, Paris
places.what: The title page of her first book gives her address as the rue Guillaume on the Isle Notre-Dame, the older name of the Île Saint-Louis. The street is now the rue Budé; the coordinates mark the modern street.

sources.title: Title page of Les Pièces de clavessin (1687), Philidor catalogue, EJG.recueil.01

places.name: Palais-Royal, Paris
places.what: First performance of her tragédie en musique by the Académie royale de musique at the Palais-Royal. Sources give 15 March (Radio France) and 17 March (IMSLP); the month is common to both.

places.name: Strasbourg
places.what: The prologue of Céphale et Procris was revived at the Académie de musique that Sébastien de Brossard had founded. This was a revival of part of the opera, and no source places her in the city.

sources.title: Catalogue de l’œuvre d’Élisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre, introduction (CMBV, Philidor)
Wikipedia coordinate record: Strasbourg

places.name: Rue Regrattière (now rue Le Regrattier), Île Saint-Louis, Paris
places.what: The 1707 title page gives her address as the rue Regrattière on the Isle Notre-Dame and lists her as one of four places of sale. The street is now the rue Le Regrattier; the coordinates mark the modern street.

sources.title: Title page of the 1707 volume, Philidor catalogue, EJG.recueil.02
Wikipedia: rue Le Regrattier (rue Regrattière from 1627), with coordinates

places.name: Château de Marly
places.work: Sonates pour le viollon et pour le clavecin
places.what: The Mercure galant of August 1707 reported that the king received her book of sonatas and harpsichord pieces at Marly, and that two days later the sonatas were played in his presence at his petit couvert. The magazine does not name the room of the performance.

sources.title: Mercure galant, August 1707, pp. 193–195, as quoted in the Philidor catalogue, EJG.recueil.02
Wikipedia coordinate record: Château de Marly

places.name: Louvre, Paris
places.what: Her Te Deum à grands chœurs was performed in the chapel of the Louvre in thanks for the recovery of Louis XV. The music is lost.

sources.title: Catherine Cessac, Elisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre, France Archives
Titon du Tillet, Le Parnasse françois (1732), entry CCXLIX, p. 636
Wikipedia coordinate record: Louvre

places.name: Saint-Eustache, Paris
places.what: Titon du Tillet stated that she was buried at Saint-Eustache. The sources consulted do not give the day of the funeral.

sources.title: Titon du Tillet, Le Parnasse françois (1732), entry CCXLIX, p. 635
